newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Universal App. buys HK$76 mln PCB unit.
newsitem.headline: Universal App. buys HK$76 mln PCB unit.

text.p: Universal Appliances Ltd has agreed to buy from its chairman Johnson Ko his entire 58.57 percent stake in printed circuit boards (PCB) maker Greatsino Electronic Ltd for HK$39.55 million, it said in a statement published on Monday.

The company also agreed to buy from PB Electonics Ltd the remaining 41.43 percent of Greatsino for HK$12.08 million, and it would pay a HK$25 million shareholder loan which Greatsino owed to PB Electronic.

Universal Appliances said the purchase from Ko would be settled by issuing 197.75 million new shares at HK$0.20 per share, and the purchase from PB Electronics would be paid by an issue of 185.39 million new shares at HK$0.20 per share.

On completion, Ko's shareholding will be diluted to 52.45 percent from 52.8 percent, while PB Electronics which previously does not hold any stake in Universal Appliances, will hold about 15 percent of the expanded share capital of the company.
PB Electronics is 51 percent owned by Paul Yap, brother of Henry Yap, a non-executive director of Universal Appliances.
Greatsino owns Greatsino Electronic Technology Ltd which has a manufacturing complex at Doumen in China's Zhuhai region to produce printed circuit boards.
The company said the purchase would vertically integrate its manufacturing operations and would enable it to enter manufacturing of high-end telecommunications products.

Meanwhile, Universal Appliances also proposed to reduce its authorised capital to HK$140 million comprising 1.40 billion shares of par value of HK$0.10 each, from HK$350 million shares comprising 1.40 billion shares of par value of HK$0.25 each.

"Given the diminution in the value of assets of the company as a result of its accumulated losses...the company's net asset value per share is significantly less than the par value of HK$0.25," the company said.
The company said implementation of the capital reduction would not alter its underlying assets, business operations, management or financial postions.
The proposed acquisitions and capital reduction is conditional on shareholders approval, it said.
Trading in the company shares, suspended last Friday, resumed on Monday. It shares were untraded at HK$0.201 in early trade. -- Hong Kong News Room (852) 2843 6370
